title: IBM Launches Unified Quantum Safe Software Suite to Automate Enterprise PQC Migration - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IBM commercially released IBM Quantum Safe at TechXchange, a three-module PQC migration suite (Explorer code scanning/CBOM, Cryptography Manager estate discovery, and a dual-protocol Proxy), timed to NIST's final migration roadmap NIST IR 8547 and federal deadlines starting in 2030. Internal validation scanned 47M+ lines of code across 5,815 repos and found 3,900+ cryptographic issues.

insights.claim: IBM has commercially released IBM Quantum Safe, a unified post-quantum cryptography migration portfolio, at its TechXchange conference, timed to coincide with NIST's final migration roadmap (NIST IR 8547).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: PQC migration tooling is now a commercial enterprise software category with IBM as an early full-stack entrant.
insights.quote: IBM has commercially released IBM Quantum Safe at its annual TechXchange conference
insights.locator: Coinciding with the publication of NIST

insights.claim: IBM Quantum Safe comprises three modules: Quantum Safe Explorer (source-code scanning and CBOM generation), Quantum Safe Cryptography Manager (estate-wide cryptographic asset discovery and posture governance), and Quantum Safe Proxy (dual-protocol mediation between legacy and PQC systems).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The discover-prioritize-mediate stack defines the template competing PQC vendors will be measured against.

insights.claim: The suite builds on IBM's 2025 deployment of Guardium Cryptography Manager, indicating IBM is extending an existing security product line rather than starting a new one.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: IBM can cross-sell PQC into its existing Guardium security customer base.
insights.quote: Building on IBM’s earlier deployment of Guardium Cryptography Manager in 2025
insights.locator: Coinciding with the publication of NIST

insights.claim: Binding federal PQC migration deadlines start in 2030, and IBM targets both commercial enterprises and government agencies needing to meet them.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hard regulatory deadlines create a multi-year, compliance-driven budget line for PQC tooling and services.
insights.quote: meeting binding federal migration deadlines starting in 2030
insights.locator: Coinciding with the publication of NIST

themes.theme: Discovery, not algorithms, is the bottleneck

insights.claim: The operational bottleneck in post-quantum migration is not the algorithms but locating vulnerable public-key dependencies across millions of lines of legacy code and sprawling hybrid IT estates.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Value in PQC migration accrues to discovery/inventory tooling and integrators, not just algorithm providers.
insights.quote: The operational bottleneck in post-quantum modernization rarely lies in the algorithms themselves

insights.claim: Running Quantum Safe Explorer internally across IBM's CIO office scanned more than 47 million lines of code in 5,815 repositories and surfaced over 3,900 cryptographic issues requiring remediation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Even a sophisticated IT organization carries thousands of crypto issues, signaling the scale of the enterprise remediation market.
insights.quote: scanning more than 47 million lines of code across 5,815 software repositories and identifying over 3,900 cryptographic issues

insights.claim: Combining automated Cryptography Bill of Materials generation with a network-level proxy lets organizations reduce 'harvest now, decrypt later' exposure for data in transit before undertaking multi-year core application rebuilds.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Proxy-based interim protection lets buyers start spending on PQC now without waiting for application refactoring.
